title: MATH GAOKAO - 154
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Principal value of the inverse sine function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate \(\arcsin\left(\frac12\right)\) using the principal range of inverse sine.
questions.question: Find the value of \(\arcsin\left(\frac12\right)\).
questions.explanation:
The principal range of \(\arcsin x\) is \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\). Since
\[
\sin\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac12
\]
and \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) lies in the principal range, we have
\[
\arcsin\left(\frac12\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}.
\]
The angle \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) also has sine \(\frac12\), but it is not in the principal range of \(\arcsin x\).
questions.hint: Recall the principal range of the inverse sine function before choosing the angle.

questions.concept: Principal value of the inverse cosine function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate \(\arccos\left(-\frac12\right)\) using the principal range of inverse cosine.
questions.question: Find the value of \(\arccos\left(-\frac12\right)\).
questions.explanation:
The principal range of \(\arccos x\) is \([0,\pi]\). Since
\[
\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}=-\frac12
\]
and \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) lies in \([0,\pi]\), we get
\[
\arccos\left(-\frac12\right)=\frac{2\pi}{3}.
\]
The angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) has cosine \(\frac12\), not \(-\frac12\).
questions.hint: Use the unit circle and remember that \(\arccos x\) returns an angle in \([0,\pi]\).

questions.concept: Principal value of the inverse tangent function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate \(\arctan(-1)\) using the principal range of inverse tangent.
questions.question: Find the value of \(\arctan(-1)\).
questions.explanation:
The principal range of \(\arctan x\) is \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). Since
\[
\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-1
\]
and \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\) lies in the principal range, we have
\[
\arctan(-1)=-\frac{\pi}{4}.
\]
The value \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) would give \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4}=1\), not \(-1\).
questions.hint: Recall that inverse tangent returns an angle between \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).

questions.concept: Composition of sine with inverse cosine
questions.question:
Find the value of
\[
\sin\left(\arccos\frac35\right).
\]
questions.explanation:
Let
\[
\theta=\arccos\frac35.
\]
Then \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\) and
\[
\cos\theta=\frac35.
\]
Because \(\cos\theta>0\), we have \(\theta\in\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), so \(\sin\theta\ge 0\). Using \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\),
\[
\sin^2\theta=1-\left(\frac35\right)^2=1-\frac{9}{25}=\frac{16}{25}.
\]
Thus
\[
\sin\theta=\frac45.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\sin\left(\arccos\frac35\right)=\frac45.
\]
questions.hint: Let \(\theta=\arccos\frac35\), then determine the sign of \(\sin\theta\) from the principal range.

questions.concept: Composition of tangent with inverse sine
questions.question:
Find the value of
\[
\tan\left(\arcsin\left(-\frac35\right)\right).
\]
questions.explanation:
Let
\[
\theta=\arcsin\left(-\frac35\right).
\]
Then \(\theta\in\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) and
\[
\sin\theta=-\frac35.
\]
Since \(\theta\) is in the principal range and \(\sin\theta<0\), we have \(\theta\in\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},0\right)\), so \(\cos\theta>0\). Using \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\),
\[
\cos^2\theta=1-\left(-\frac35\right)^2=1-\frac{9}{25}=\frac{16}{25}.
\]
Thus
\[
\cos\theta=\frac45.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}
=\frac{-\frac35}{\frac45}
=-\frac34.
\]
questions.hint: Determine the sign of \(\cos\theta\) from the principal range of \(\arcsin x\), then use \(\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\).

questions.concept: Inverse cosine of a cosine value outside the principal interval
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate \(\arccos\left(\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\) using the principal range of inverse cosine.
questions.question:
Find the value of
\[
\arccos\left(\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}\right).
\]
questions.explanation:
First,
\[
\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
We need the angle in \([0,\pi]\) whose cosine is \(-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\). That angle is
\[
\frac{5\pi}{6}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\arccos\left(\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{5\pi}{6}.
\]
The value \(\frac{7\pi}{6}\) is not in the principal range \([0,\pi]\) of \(\arccos x\).
questions.hint: Find \(\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}\) first, then choose the angle in \([0,\pi]\) with that cosine.

questions.concept: Cosine of a sum of inverse trigonometric angles
questions.question:
Find the value of
\[
\cos\left(\arcsin\frac{5}{13}+\arccos\frac35\right).
\]
questions.explanation:
Let
\[
\alpha=\arcsin\frac{5}{13},\qquad \beta=\arccos\frac35.
\]
Then
\[
\sin\alpha=\frac{5}{13},\qquad \cos\beta=\frac35.
\]
Since both principal angles lie in the first quadrant,
\[
\cos\alpha=\frac{12}{13},\qquad \sin\beta=\frac45.
\]
Using the cosine addition formula,
\[
\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\cos\alpha\cos\beta-\sin\alpha\sin\beta.
\]
Thus
\[
\cos(\alpha+\beta)
=\frac{12}{13}\cdot\frac35-\frac{5}{13}\cdot\frac45
=\frac{36}{65}-\frac{20}{65}
=\frac{16}{65}.
\]
questions.hint: Let \(\alpha=\arcsin\frac{5}{13}\) and \(\beta=\arccos\frac35\), then find the missing sine and cosine values.

questions.question:
Find the value of
\[
\sin\left(2\arctan\frac12\right).
\]
questions.explanation:
Let
\[
\theta=\arctan\frac12.
\]
Then
\[
\tan\theta=\frac12.
\]
Using the double-angle identity
\[
\sin 2\theta=\frac{2\tan\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta},
\]
we get
\[
\sin 2\theta
=\frac{2\cdot\frac12}{1+\left(\frac12\right)^2}
=\frac{1}{1+\frac14}
=\frac{1}{\frac54}
=\frac45.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\sin\left(2\arctan\frac12\right)=\frac45.
\]
questions.hint: Use the double-angle formula for sine in terms of \(\tan\theta\).

questions.concept: Solving an equation involving inverse sine and inverse cosine
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(\arccos x=\arcsin x\) using principal ranges.
questions.question:
Solve
\[
\arccos x=\arcsin x.
\]
questions.explanation:
Let
\[
\theta=\arccos x=\arcsin x.
\]
Since \(\arccos x\in[0,\pi]\) and \(\arcsin x\in\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), we have
\[
\theta\in\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right].
\]
The equation gives
\[
\cos\theta=\sin\theta.
\]
Thus
\[
\tan\theta=1,
\]
so
\[
\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
x=\cos\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}.
\]
questions.hint: Use the common angle \(\theta\) and note that it must lie in both principal ranges.

questions.learningObjective: Determine \(y\) from \(\arcsin x+\arcsin y=\frac{\pi}{2}\) using complementary angles.
questions.explanation:
Let
\[
\alpha=\arcsin x,\qquad \beta=\arcsin y.
\]
Then
\[
\alpha+\beta=\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]
Thus
\[
\beta=\frac{\pi}{2}-\alpha.
\]
Taking sine on both sides,
\[
y=\sin\beta=\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\alpha\right)=\cos\alpha.
\]
Since \(\alpha=\arcsin x\), we have
\[
\sin\alpha=x.
\]
Because \(x\in[0,1]\), \(\alpha\in\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), so \(\cos\alpha\ge 0\). Therefore,
\[
\cos\alpha=\sqrt{1-\sin^2\alpha}=\sqrt{1-x^2}.
\]
Hence
\[
y=\sqrt{1-x^2}.
\]
questions.hint: Let \(\alpha=\arcsin x\) and \(\beta=\arcsin y\), then use the complementary-angle identity.
